name: Elephantfolk
body:
Image used by permission of d20pfsrd.com Publishing

These large humanoids with elephantine features are known by many different names in many different parts of the world: elephantfolk, mammothfolk, oliphauntans, loxodonts, pachydermians, and many more.

Regardless of the name they are called by, they are almost universally respected for their wisdom and steady demeanor.

Physical

Elephantfolk are large bipedal humanoids with elephant-like heads, including wide ears, trunk-like noses, and ivory tusks. They have broad, flat feet like elephants, the better to support their weight, but their hands are surprisingly small and delicate, allowing them to easily handle most tools sized for humans.

Elephantfolk have thick, wrinkled skin that is only sparsely covered with coarse hair. Their skin tends to be gray or grayish-blue, sometimes lightening to pink or white on the ears and trunk. However, some elephantfolk have been described with more exotic coloration, such as forest green, solid black, or bright pink.

Social

Most elephantfolk are peaceful, gentle beings. They live in small communities, which they call herds. Some of these herds are itinerant, but most have settled into forming small villages or neighborhoods within larger settlements among humans or other humanoids.

Elephantfolk are not fully grown until age 40, at which time they ae considered fully mature adults. Until this time, they are considered youths, and most spend this period in study and apprenticeship to their herd.

Elephantfolk are renowned for their wisdom, and many spend their entire lives in pursuit of greater understanding. They are highly communal, and love sharing their thoughts, opinions, and discoveries with others. Many work as teachers in human cities, or travel the world as bards or philosophers.

Alignment and Religion

By and large, elephantfolk are of Good alignment, being raised in their herds to have a strong sense of compassion and understanding for all creatures. Most are also Lawful, as the traditions and sense of obligation comes naturally to them. However, there is also a strong contingent of elephantfolk who feel the sense of wanderlust, and among these individuals there are many who feel a need for more autonomy and the trend of Chaotic alignments is more pronounced.

Elephantfolk do not have deities of their own, but instead have their own monastic and philosophical traditions. However, many do observe the religions of their human neighbors, often in conjunction with their own traditional spiritual practices.

Names

Some common elephantfolk names include the following (choose or roll 1d12):

Drobikana
Hakti
Hatishali
Iroja
Lavidanta
Nakio
Runjeepa
Sashano
Sfirya
Varijani
Vartunya
Vashigula
Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are sturdy and wise, by not well-coordinated. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Con, +2 Wis, –2 Dex [standard]. (0)
Note: After your modifiers for being size Large are incorporated, your net ability score modifiers are: +2 Str, +2 Con, +2 Wis, –4 Dex.
Size As a Large creature, you have a –1 size penalty on attack rolls, a –1 size penalty to your Armor Class, a +1 size bonus to your CMB, and a –4 size penalty on Stealth checks. As a Large creature, you occupy a space of 10 feet by 10 feet. Your reach is 5 feet. You take a further –2 penalty to Dex, and gain a further +2 bonus to Str. (7)
Type Humanoid. You are a Humanoid with the elephantfolk subtype. (0)
Speed Your base speed is 30 feet. (0)
Languages You begin play speaking Common and Sylvan. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Celestial, Draconic, Elven, Giant, and Gnoll. (0)
Other Traits
Eternal Hope You gain a +2 species bonus on saving throws against fear and despair effects. Also, once per day, after a natural roll of 1 on a d20 roll, you may reroll and use the second result. (2)
Senses Low-light vision. You can see twice as far as a human in starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar conditions of poor illumination. You retain the ability to distinguish color and detail under these conditions. (1)
Natural Armor You have tough, resilient skin that provides a +2 natural armor bonus. (3)
Trunk You have a flexible trunk that you can use to make an attack; this is a secondary natural attack that deals 1d6 bludgeoning damage. Alternatively, you can use your trunk to carry objects. You cannot wield a weapon or shield with your trunk, but you can retrieve a small, stowed objects carried on your person as a swift action. (3)
Undersized Grip Your hands are small compared to your immense body, making it difficult for you to wield properly-sized weapons. As such, your ability to wield manufactured weapons is determined as though you were one size category smaller than you actually are—size Medium instead of Large. (–2)
Total: 14 RP (Advanced)
Variants
Elephantfolk Bully

You’re big and strong, and you know how to throw your weight around. Your net ability scores (including the adjustments for being size Large) are +4 Str, +2 Cha, –2 Dex, –2 Int. This alters ability score modifiers.

Erudite Elephantfolk

Having spent your youth with your trunk in a book, or discussing current events with high society, you are knowledgeable and gifted at conversation, but not as hearty or as hands-on as most of your kin. Your net ability scores (including the adjustments for being size Large) are +2 Str, +2 Int, +2 Cha, –4 Dex. This alters ability score modifiers.

Alternate Species Traits
Extra Trunk You have a rare mutation that gives you not one but two trunks. Each of these can be used to deliver a secondary natural attack (1d6 damage) or manipulate objects, just as a single trunk could do. This trait alters trunk and replaces eternal hope.
Sensitive Trunk Your trunk gives you a highly attuned sense of smell. You have the scent B1 universal monster ability. This trait replaces trunk.
Psychic Trunk You can use detect psychic significance and mindlink once each per day as spell-like abilities. You must touch the object or creature with your trunk in order to use these abilities. You use your character level as the caster level for these abilities, and Charisma is your casting ability. In addition, your trunk functions as a dowsing rod, and you can use the dowsing psychic skill unlock one extra time per day. (If you cannot normally use psychic skill unlocks, you gain one daily use of the dowsing psychic skill unlock.) This trait replaces eternal hope.
Favored Class Bonuses
Alchemist Add one extract formula from the alchemist’s list to your formula book. This formula must be at least one level lower than the highest level of alchemist formula you can create.
Bard Add +1/2 to your bardic knowledge bonus.
Cleric Select one domain power granted at 1st level that is normally usable a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Wisdom modifier. Add +1/2 to the number of uses per day of that domain power.
Fighter Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a bull rush or overrun attempt.
Investigator Add one extract formula from the investigator’s list to your formula book. This formula must be at least one level lower than the highest level of investigator formula you can create.
Mesmerist Increase the number of mesmerist tricks you can use per day by +1/3.
Monk Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a grapple or bull rush attempt.
Occultist Gain +1/6 of a new focus power.
Oracle Add +1/6 to your effective oracle level for the purpose of determining the effects of one revelation.
Paladin Add +1/2 hit point to your lay on hands ability (whether using it to heal or harm).
Psychic Increase the total number of points in your phrenic pool by +1/3 point.
Scholar Add a +1/3 bonus to your inspiration rolls.
Sorcerer Select one bloodline power at 1st level that is normally usable a number of times per day equal to 3 +your Charisma modifier. Add +1/2 to the number of uses per day of that bloodline power.
